segments.text: Meet Aha: two skills that help your AI agent investigate a difficult question and create a visual explanation.
The goal is not just a longer answer. It is something another person can explore, present, or watch.
Take noise-cancelling headphones. Why does the rumble fade while voices remain? This existing web example combines a diagram with a phase-mismatch slider.
Readers can explore an ideal model. We are showing a screenshot, not measuring a real pair of headphones.
Or take Git merge. How can a merge bring back a reverted change? Another existing web explanation puts history, files, and results together.
Readers switch between three recorded cases to compare what happened. This is an explanation of saved results, not a live Git run.
Start with your question and your audience. Aha guides the agent to investigate sources, keep evidence and open questions, then design the explanation for the chosen medium.
Use the research skill for a report, or the explanation skill for a visual artifact, with research when needed.
Choose the experience your reader needs. An interactive web page to explore. A single image to scan. Editable slides to present. Or a narrated video to watch.
Each requested format is authored for its purpose, rather than automatically converting one finished piece into all the others.
That is Aha: research the question, design the explanation, and give people something they can use. Think of learning a difficult idea, explaining a codebase, or sharing what you found.
Review the sources and the finished work, then judge whether your audience can actually understand it.
